evidence_debug.research:
To let users sign in to your web application using their Google account, you can implement **Google Identity Services**, which conforms to the OpenID Connect (OIDC) standard. 

Here is an overview of the steps required to configure and integrate Google Sign-In into your web app:

### 1. Configure a Project in Google Cloud
1. Go to the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/).
2. Create a new project or select an existing one.
3. Navigate to **APIs & Services** > **OAuth consent screen**. Configure your application name, support email, and user scopes (such as `email` and `profile`).
4. Go to **APIs & Services** > **Credentials**:
   * Click **Create Credentials** and choose **OAuth client ID**.
   * Select **Web application** as the application type.
   * Add your app's origin domains to **Authorized JavaScript origins** and your callback/redirect URLs to **Authorized redirect URIs**.
5. Retrieve your generated **Client ID** (and **Client Secret** if performing server-side validation).

---

### 2. Implementation Options
You can implement Google Sign-In either via frontend client libraries or standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization flows:

* **Google Identity Services JavaScript Library (Recommended for Websites):**
  Embeds the official "Sign in with Google" button and handles token generation seamlessly on the client side.
  * *Authorization Endpoint:* `https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth`
  * *Token Endpoint:* `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token`
  * *OIDC Discovery Document:* `https://accounts.google.com/.well-known/openid-configuration`

* **Handling the Token:**
  Upon successful authentication, Google returns an OpenID Connect **ID Token** (a JWT) to your application. Your frontend or backend can verify this token's signature using Google's public keys available at the JWKS URI (`https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs`) to securely identify the user.
